chunks: And when a Surah is revealed, some of them look at others, asking: 'Is anyone looking at us?' Then they turn away. God has turned their hearts away because they are a people who do not understand.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Quraysh leaders look at each other when the Quran was revealed?
ai.summary: This verse, from Surah At-Tawbah (9:67), illustrates the psychological state of the Quraysh elite who, upon hearing the Quran, glanced at one another to gauge social perception and avoid ridicule, ultimately turning away in spiritual blindness. Shia exegetes, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, emphasize that 'God has turned their hearts' signifies a divine consequence of their persistent arrogance and lack of deep comprehension (faqh), rather than mere predestination. This reaction underscores the theme of *ghurur* (self-deception) where external validation outweighs internal truth, a key concept in understanding the Quraysh's rejection of prophethood.
